title: Return a result
summary: Rust: Return a result. Call twice(7). Try a small example and check what happens.
introduction: The last expression can be a function result. It has no trailing semicolon.

blocks.text: Install stable Rust. Save each example as lesson.rs, run rustc lesson.rs, then run the created program.

blocks.title: Return a result
blocks.code:
fn twice(n: i32) -> i32 { n * 2 }
fn main() { println!("{}", twice(4)); }

blocks.text: The input n becomes 4. Without a trailing semicolon, n * 2 is returned.

blocks.title: Watch out
blocks.text: A semicolon after n * 2 turns it into a statement with no returned number.
